source.title: Pathways of Visual Information Flow in Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Israfel Salazar; Stella Frank; Dan Oneata; Desmond Elliott; Constanza Fierro

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether VLMs can reroute visual information after attention-path knockouts, extending the backup/compensation question to vision-language models and pathway-level interventions. It does not ablate individual attention layers or heads.
record.gate_note: The paper measures pathway-level routing and task accuracy, not changes in later components' outputs or restoration of a prediction relative to a component's direct effect. The principal relevant results are direct-pathway attention knockouts and text-token recovery under corrupted-image patching. It also reports knockouts of the text-mediated pathway, but those test pathway necessity rather than compensation after ablating the direct route; those results are not itemized here.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It knocks out attention edges between token groups (image→last token) at all layers at once in VLMs, and measures task accuracy and pathway usage. It does not ablate single attention layers, heads or MLPs, and it does not measure later components' outputs changing to restore the prediction. That rerouting is a related but different construct, so it belongs under fits_no_version. The paper also links its result to backup-circuit and Hydra work, claiming 'almost full rerouting' versus partial compensation in text models. That link is a discussion point, not a test of V1–V7. The reader's 'tests/T3' conflicts with its own finding that every version is not_tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Two additions: the authors call this a stronger form than text-only backup circuits ('almost full rerouting' rather than partial compensation). They also say knockouts answer necessity while causal patching answers usage, so the two must be combined.
record.recipe_differences: Uses token-group causal patching, corrupted-image patching, and attention-edge knockouts in VLMs; it does not ablate individual attention layers or heads as in the original self-repair studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Pathway use varies with task, data distribution, prompt format, and model family. Recognition shifts toward text mediation under choices prompts; localization routing differs between synthetic and natural data, with a model-family difference for localization.

fits_no_version.finding: Blocking image→last-token attention at all layers leaves accuracy largely intact across three VLMs (e.g., Qwen 0.0 pp on synthetic tasks, up to +13.6 pp for InternVL on VG_QA_one). Paired causal patching shows recognition normally uses that direct route. Text-token representations alone recover answers when the image is replaced by noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In VLMs, knocking out the normally used direct visual pathway triggers near-full rerouting through a text-mediated pathway. Attention-knockout necessity therefore misstates pathway usage, a pathway-level analogue of self-repair and of V7.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the knockout deltas or patching metrics. Interventions operate on token groups or attention edges rather than individual attention heads/layers or MLP components. Natural-data patching is restricted to pairs on which the model answers both examples correctly; results are task- and dataset-dependent.
record.rows_left_out: The per-dataset knockouts of the text-mediated paths (rI→T and rT→last) in Appendix Tables 16–18 are omitted because they measure dependence on those paths, not fallback after direct-pathway ablation. Per-dataset patching curves and additional corruption-type checks in Appendix Figures 9–11 and Tables 8, 15 are also omitted; the main aggregate corrupted-patching results are included.

untested.parts: No single attention layer is ablated. Knockouts block token-group attention edges in all layers at once.
No MLP layers or erasure of the max-likelihood token are measured.
No individual heads are ablated. Tasks are narrow single-token VQA, not general text.
No per-prompt compensation distribution or overcorrection measure for component ablation.
No backup heads, copy-suppression heads, LayerNorm or neurons are identified. Head/MLP localization is left to future work.
No mean or resample ablation. Knockouts use -inf attention masking; corruption uses noise, black or white images.

No component-level ablation importance scores. The paper does argue that pathway knockouts misstate usage (recognition uses the direct path, yet knocking it out costs 0.0 pp on Qwen), but at the level of a token-group route.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites McGrath et al. (Hydra) and McDougall et al. only as background. Not all knockout results are negligible: Qwen Controlled CLEVR drops 9.6 pp and LLaVA Shapes Localization drops 5.5 pp. No uncertainty estimates are reported. If curators later broaden V7 to route-level interventions, the recognition case (direct-path usage from patching versus 0.0 pp knockout effect) would bear on it.

versions.untested_parts: No attention layer is ablated; the interventions block attention edges between token groups.
No late MLP layers or maximum-likelihood-token erasure are measured.
No individual attention heads are ablated, and the study does not measure head-level compensation on the full distribution.
The study does not measure prompt-level variation or overcorrection in component self-repair.
No backup heads, copy-suppression heads, LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons are identified.
The study does not test mean or resample ablations. Its uniform-noise, black, and white corrupted-image conditions are not on-distribution component ablations.
It discusses limits of interpreting ablation-based interventions, but does not compute ablation-based component importance scores.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-4B
rows.operation_detail: Patched all-layer text-token representations from a clean inference while the input image was uniform noise.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as text representations carrying sufficient visual information, including for tasks normally routed directly.
rows.check: r31–r44 are corrupted-image text patching. They show the text route is sufficient when the image is noise. They do not measure compensation after a component ablation, and they compare no clean ablation baseline.
